column2: Ishvara, in this your authority I shall initiate the seeker of liberation; be favorable to us — so he should make the announcement.
Having done the invocation of the parents, the striking of the disciple and the rest, having taken the consciousness one should unite it to the Self by rule.
As before having imagined the union of the parents, with the one called rising, with the self-seed enclosed by the heart, one should place it in the goddess's womb.
In the arising of the body five with the heart, with the head for the cause of birth, with the crest for authority, with the armor-atom for enjoyment,
with the weapon-mantra for dissolution, with Shiva for the purification of channels, with the heart for the purification of principles — thus impregnation and the rest as before.
With armor for the loosening of the bond, having thus atoned one should repeat a hundred; five oblations with the weapon for hiding the power of impurity.
Likewise for the separation of the bond, then with the seven-weapon-consecrated weapon, with scissors one should cut the bonds with the seed.
Om Haum, to the bond of the digit Shanti, Hah Hum phat — having released, made round with the bond-mantra as before, having put in a ladle full of ghee, one should offer with the digit-weapon alone;
one should offer five with the weapon for release from noose and goad; for the prevention of expiation one should then give eight oblations:
Om Hah, to the weapon, Hum phat. Having invoked Ishvara in the heart and done worship and satisfaction, by rule one should make the offering of fee to him:
Om Ham, Ishvara, accept intellect and ego as fee, svaha; this beast whose bonds are all burnt, Ishvara, by you he should not stay as binding — so one should have Shiva's command heard.
One should dismiss Ishvara the god and join the Rudra-self; one should unite the Self like a slight moon to the Self by rule.
One should join it to the thread by the purified rising mudra; with the root-mantra one should give a nectar-drop on the disciple's head.
Having dismissed the parents of the fire worshipped with flowers and the rest, one who knows the rule should give the full oblation completing all rites.
Here too striking and the rest should be done as before; with one's own seed there is the distinction; purification is not hindered by peace.
With head and neck extended, following the utterance of nada, even-visioned, Shiva within, endowed with supreme feeling,
from the pot, mandala and fire, from the disciple and from one's own self, having taken the sixfold rule, at the tip of the ladle the channel of breath,
having contemplated it like a bindu, meditating in order sevenfold: the first the form of union with breath, then another,
released by the order of utterance beginning with the heart, called mantra; having done inhalation and retention, opening the mouth slightly,
the third, following the Sushumna, of the nature of nada; in the seventh, from abandoning the cause, the dissolution of the quiet vikhara.
The upward movement of power and nada is held the power-vikhara; of all breath, free of what power can measure,
the sixth is the time-vikhara, and the seventh beyond power; this is the place of union called principle-vikhara.
Having done inhalation and retention and opening the mouth slightly, slowly uttering the root, making the dissolution of the disciple's self,
in the letter Ha, lightning-shaped, of the nature of the breath of the six paths; the letter U beyond, a span above the navel, pervading;
then beyond that the letter Ma four fingers from the heart; Om, denoting Vishnu; then the throat eight fingers;
Ma at the palate four fingers, denoting Rudra; likewise the bindu in the middle of the forehead denoting Ishvara;
nada, the god Sadashiva, ending at the Brahma-aperture; and the power standing at the Brahma-aperture, continually leaving in order,
having experienced there the divine touch of an ant, in the supreme principle at the twelve-end, of the mark of supreme bliss,
in Shiva free of feeling, beyond mind, in whom the eternal qualities arise, dissolved in that mind one should contemplate the disciple's Self.
Releasing the stream of ghee even at the flame-end, in the supreme Shiva, for the steadiness of the union, with the Shiva-atom ending in vaushat,

having given the full oblation by rule one should perform the "conferring of qualities": "Om Ham, to the Self, be omniscient, svaha. Om Ham, to the Self, be fully satisfied, svaha. Om Hrum, to the Self, be of beginningless awareness, svaha. Om Haum, to the Self, be independent, svaha. Om Haum, to the Self, be of unfailing power, svaha. Om Hah, to the Self, be of infinite power, svaha." Thus having taken the Self of six qualities from the supreme imperishable,
endowed with contemplation, by rule one should unite it in the disciple's body. For the quieting of fatigue produced by the falling of intense atomic power,
one should place on the disciple's head a drop of nectar from the arghya. Having had him bow to Ishvara's pot and the rest, in the right circle of Shiva,
having seated the disciple on one's right with face gentle: "By you alone this one is favored, having taken my form;
increase his devotion also to the god, the fire and the teacher." Having thus informed the lord of the gods, and having bowed, the teacher himself

should say "May there be good for you" with respect to the disciple. Then with supreme devotion, having given eight flowers to the god, having bathed the boy with Shiva's pot, one should dismiss the sacrifice.
In the middle one should place Shiva, the ocean and the Shiva-mantra. In the bath-pavilion set up as the sacrificial hall of the lord of the quarter,
one should make an altar two cubits long and eight fingers high. Having placed there on a seat of shriparna and the rest "Anantamanasa,"
having seated the disciple facing east, having made him complete, one should worship. With sour gruel, boiled rice, clay, ash, durva and cow-dung balls,
with mustard, curds and water, one should then do the cleansing. Then in order with alkaline water, with the heart and the lords of knowledge,
one should bathe the disciple with pots, with svadha-holding; having clothed him in white garments and seated him on Shiva's right,
on the seat stated before one should again worship the disciple as before: turban, yoga-band, crown, scissors, pot,
rosary, book and the rest — authority over Shiva and so on: "Knowing initiation, exposition, installation and the rest, from today by you
it is to be done after careful examination" — so one should have the command heard. Having then greeted the disciple and bowed to Maheshvara,
for removing the flame of obstacles one should make the petition thus: "I have been commanded by you in the form of the teacher for the anointing;
this one, master of the Samhita, has been anointed by me, Shiva." One should offer five and five oblations for the satisfaction of the mantra-circle;
then give the full oblation; one should seat the disciple on one's right. The fingers beginning with the thumb on the disciple's right hand in order
one should mark for the one bound with burnt darbha tips; having placed flowers in the hand one should have him bow:
In pot, fire, Shiva, and oneself, may he enter that work. Disciples well examined by scripture are to be favored by you.
Like kings, of men and others the desired comes by anointing: "Am Shram Shraum, the beast, Hum phat" — from the anointing with the king of weapons.
Granting knowledge of past and future, mantra, intellect, enjoyment and liberation; having taken the subtle letters of the question, with two the good and bad,
with three the individual and root element, with four the thought of Brahmins and others; and the elements and principles at first, in the rest repetition and the rest.
At the end of one and three, in the word with the last of two... inauspicious, middling in the middles; in three, Indra, king, auspicious.
In the group of numbers the span of life; Yama is the destroyer of ten years surely; one should write on a lotus with the mantras of the Sun, Ganesha, Durga, Shri and Vishnu.
When touched with consecrated Kathini by lines in the form of cow's urine, beginning with one up to three, ending with three-four,
by the wind, space, and wind-seeds in the sixty-four-square, likewise; from the falling of dice and touching, on odd and the rest, auspicious and the rest.
Beginning with one and three, and at the end eight and three; the banners and the rest even, defective, odd, give the beautiful and the rest.
With the consonants beginning with Ka, sprouted, preceded by the sixteen vowels; with those with vowels, the Tripura-name mantras.
With the seed Hrim, beginning with Om, ending in namah, where worship is done; the mantras twenty thousand, then a hundred and sixty more.
The "Am Hrim" mantras of Sarasvati and of Chandika likewise; likewise of Gauri and Durga; "Am Shrim" mantras of Shri;
likewise "Ksham Krom" mantras of the Sun, "Am Haum" mantras of Shiva; "Am Gam" mantras of Ganesha; and "Am" mantras of Hari.
With fifty-one consonants beginning with Ka, and sixteen vowels, with those with vowels, with the last consonants — all mantras thus.

Of Sun, Ishvara, Goddess and Vishnu by the arrangement of their own sea, god and Indra, three hundred and sixty each mandala in order. Having been anointed, one should repeat and meditate; the teacher should initiate disciples and others.
This giving of arghya is told, by the turning of the pot there. Thus one should take possession of the land afterward,
up to gravel or up to water, wishing to destroy the fault of foreign objects. If one has the earth dug by a maiden, one should remove the foreign object by rule.
The question-letters if the man — A, Ka, Cha, Ta, Ta, Pa, Ya, Sha, Ha — fallen as banners and the rest of Agni, state a foreign object in its own place;
and by the maker's bodily change one should know by that measure; by the entry of animals and the rest, by announcements, by cries, the directions.
One should write the matrix of letters rich in eight groups on a board or on the ground; knowledge of foreign matter by group from east to northeast in order:
in the A group iron; in the Ka group charcoal from the fire; in the Cha group ash in the south; in the Ta group bone in the southwest;
in the Ta group brick; in the west; skull in the Pa group; in the Ya group a corpse's remains and the rest; in the Sha group one should indicate iron;
in the Ha group silver; likewise even from the group-less harmful things. Having examined with handfuls with earth of eight finger-breadths between,
having filled the dug pit to a quarter less with water, struck with pestles, the teacher having had the ground plastered and leveled there,
with ordinary arghya in hand one should go to the pavilion to be described; having worshipped the lords of the arches and doors, one should enter by the west door.
There one should do self-purification and the rest, the preparation of the pit and pavilion; the pot with Vardhani attached, worship of the guardians and Shiva,
the generation and worship of fire and the rest — all as before. With the sacrificer one should go to the bathing pavilion of the stones.
The stones of the temple and linga named Pada, Dharma and so on, are praised as eight fingers high, square, a cubit long;
the stones for stone temples; of bricks half that; in a stone temple stone slabs, on a hill bricks, in a brick one bricks.
Marked with nine-faced and other marks, lotus-marked with lotuses: Nanda, Bhadra, Jaya, Rikta, Purna the fifth are held.
Of these Padma, Mahapadma, Shankha, then Makara, and Samudra — these five treasure-pots in order below.
Nanda, Bhadra, Jaya, Purna, Ajita, Aparajita, Vijaya, Mangala, and Dharani the ninth stone.
